notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-5: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus run, all rc 0, head c1bf437, uncommitted true and one skill_hash (33324d7b...); the hash recomputed over the repository's idiomatic-elixir/ folder and over the run root's skill copy gives the same digest, so the runs read the current working-tree text, including the uncommitted sentences (the `if` 60-character limit, "Applying a rule or a finding", the `==` sentence in Match every expected shape). Every transcript contains "unless the clauses read as a table", "the whole `if` fits in about 60 characters", "is a match written as a comparison" and "An `else` whose every clause returns the same value". Each transcript's assistant messages name only the tier model; the two claude-fable-5-1 strings per transcript are the advisor-tool attachment, which no run called. Every session was shown 62 skills. Reads: haiku-2 SKILL.md and library-design.md; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests, run from the compiled beams: haiku-1 none, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3 (sonnet-2's final message says it could not run them; they pass).

Changed rules: git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes four of the ten graded rules. Put each `->` body on its own line unless the clauses read as a table (renamed from "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line"): the sentence that decides a verdict here is "A row that calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, does not read that way, because one row gives an answer and the other hands off"; it makes haiku-2 violated (lines 142-143 and 149-150), and haiku-1's inline rows stay clean because every row gives an answer of one mapping ("the rows line up as alternatives of one mapping"), the longest 58 characters after the indentation. Match every expected shape (new sentences on different reasons and on `==` against a built tuple), Chain fallible steps with `with` (step failures in the holding function's shape; an `else` whose every clause returns one value; "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function") and Return `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` (a lookup whose only failure is absence may return nil) changed too, but no run has the shapes those sentences address (every run gives missing and invalid fields different reasons, has no `else`, no nested `case` in a `with` body and no nil-returning step), so they decide nothing here. Also changed, outside the list: the do: rule's `if` limit and the "Applying a rule or a finding" bullet. The unchanged rules are held to the 2026-10-31-b standard.

Batch items. One-line `if ..., do: ..., else: ...`: none in any run (haiku-2's only `if`, line 155: if valid?.(value) do, is a block). `==` comparing a call result with a tuple or map built in place: none; the only `==` is haiku-2 line 164: defp currency_code?(value), do: is_binary(value) and byte_size(value) == 3, an integer literal with the checked value on the left. The code-review item does not apply to this case.

Closest calls. Read required keys, haiku-2: optional/3 (line 148: case Map.get(data, key) do) reads customer_email and failure_reason, which Payment lists in @enforce_keys (line 24); held clean because the parser's contract makes both keys optional (line 149: nil -> {:ok, nil}; @type gives String.t() | nil; the @moduledoc says failure_reason is nil unless the provider sends one), and @enforce_keys here only makes the constructor pass nil explicitly. The 2026-10-31-b grades used absence from @enforce_keys as enough to call a key optional, not presence as enough to call it required. Struct rule and head check, haiku-1: the parse/1 head (line 75) matches only "type" and "data", unlike every earlier run, and reads "id" and "created" with Map.fetch through string_field/2 and integer_field/2 inside the with, so a missing id gives {:missing_field, "id"} (verified); held clean and the head check met, because that is the per-field route the struct rule gives ("check the fields one at a time in small functions chained with `with`, each returning `{:error, {:missing_field, key}}`"), not a bracket read checked for nil. Match every expected shape: haiku-1 event_kind/1, haiku-2 parse_type/1 and sonnet-1 parse_type/1 have no is_binary guard, so "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}; kept in checks, as 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b kept the same shape (counted, Haiku and Sonnet would be violated); sonnet-2 lines 115-116 answer {:invalid_field, "type"}. Multi-clause: haiku-1 parse_data/2 (lines 93-95) and sonnet-2 parse_data/2 (lines 130, 132, 139) bind data in all three clauses for the body only; held clean as positional arguments, not fields bound from a matched value, as 2026-10-31-b held haiku-1's build/4. Outside the list: sonnet-1's parse_data/2 mixes a block (lines 140-143, head wrapped after a long guard) with do: clauses (lines 145-146), not counted, as 2026-10-31-b held the same mix in sonnet-1; the multi-line {:ok, %Payment{...}} returns in sonnet-1 (lines 154-161) and sonnet-2 (lines 151-157) are return values, not call arguments, not counted under Build a multi-line argument, as before.

Probe of 28 payloads (known types, unknown type, integer and missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing customer_email and payment_id, missing and integer failure_reason on payment.failed, missing refund fields, a string amount on a refund, string and out-of-range created, missing and integer id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all four: payment.succeeded, payment.failed and refund.created parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a string amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a nil amount or currency gives {:invalid_field, key}; a missing type or data, or a non-map payload, gives :invalid_payload. Differences: a missing id or created gives {:missing_field, key} in haiku-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; "id" => 5 gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and :invalid_payload in haiku-2; "type" => 123 gives {:invalid_field, "type"} only in sonnet-2; list data gives {:invalid_field, "data"} in sonnet-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; a negative amount and an integer failure_reason are accepted only by haiku-1, which checks amount with is_integer alone and copies customer_email and failure_reason unchecked with Map.get; a missing customer_email is rejected only by sonnet-2.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31-b at 74112b4): Opus has no run in this batch. The `->` rule moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-2's hand-off rows), a move the rewritten text decides; under the old text's "one returning a finished value while another continues the computation" the same lines would also have broken, so the move is between runs as much as between texts. Comments moves from Sonnet violated to clean (no wrong doctest timestamp; sonnet-1's three doctests pass). Read required keys, Match every expected shape, the multi-clause rule, atoms, the with rule, the return-tuple rule, the struct rule and Naming stay clean in both tiers.
